precepts.text: Isaiah prophesied to Hezekiah that all in his house and the treasures his fathers had laid up would be carried to Babylon, fulfilled in this robbing of the temple.
precepts.point: He carried Jehoiachin, the king's mother, wives, and officers to Babylon, along with the men of might and craftsmen and smiths, wanting them to build for him what they had built in their own land, as conquering nations always used Israel's skill and industry.

note.label: 2 Kings 24: Judah Carried Away for the Sins of Manasseh

precepts.why:
Isaiah told Hezekiah, “Behold, the days come, that all that is in thine house, and that which thy fathers have laid up in store until this day, shall be carried to Babylon: nothing shall be left, saith the Lord.”

Here it is fulfilled. Nebuchadnezzar “carried out thence all the treasures of the house of the Lord, and the treasures of the king’s house, and cut in pieces all the vessels of gold which Solomon king of Israel had made in the temple of the Lord, as the Lord had said.” The robbing of the temple is exactly what Isaiah prophesied: nothing left.

And not only the treasures. He carried away all Jerusalem, the princes, the mighty men of valour, ten thousand captives, “and all the craftsmen and smiths: none remained, save the poorest sort of the people of the land.” Jehoiachin, the king’s mother, his wives and his officers went to Babylon too. Babylon wanted the craftsmen and smiths to build for it what they had built in their own land, for conquering nations have always used Israel’s skill and industry.

precepts.text: The word about sons made eunuchs in Babylon points forward to Daniel, a eunuch in the palace of the king of Babylon.
precepts.point: The prophecy adds that Hezekiah's own sons that issue from him would be taken and made eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon. Hezekiah called the word of the Lord good because there would be peace and truth in his days.

note.label: Isaiah 39: The Treasures Shown and Babylon Foretold

precepts.why:
Isaiah told Hezekiah, “of thy sons that shall issue from thee, which thou shalt beget, shall they take away; and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.” Daniel shows it come to pass: “Now among these were of the children of Judah, Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah”.

The word about sons made eunuchs in Babylon points forward to Daniel, of the children of Judah, a eunuch in the palace of the king of Babylon. Everything Hezekiah showed the men from Babylon, the silver, the gold, the spices, the ointment and all his armour, holding nothing back, was carried to Babylon with nothing left, and his sons went with it, just as Isaiah declared. Hezekiah called the word good because “there shall be peace and truth in my days”, but the days came.

precepts.text: Because Hezekiah showed Babylon all his treasures, the days would come when all in his house would be carried to Babylon and nothing would be left.
precepts.point: This was a billion dollar heist of the temple's gold, brass, and silver, and it too was prophecy; it fulfilled what was foretold to Hezekiah when he foolishly showed Babylon all his treasures.

note.label: Jeremiah 52: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Puppet King Zedekiah

precepts.why:
Hezekiah foolishly showed Babylon all his treasures, and Isaiah told him: “Behold, the days come, that all that is in thine house, and that which thy fathers have laid up in store until this day, shall be carried to Babylon: nothing shall be left, saith the Lord. And of thy sons that shall issue from thee, which thou shalt beget, shall they take away; and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.”

That is what Nebuzaradan finished. The Chaldeans broke the pillars of brass, the bases, and the brazen sea in the house of the Most High and carried all the brass to Babylon, along with the caldrons, shovels, snuffers, bowls, spoons, and every vessel of brass, gold, and silver; “that which was of gold in gold, and that which was of silver in silver, took the captain of the guard away.” Nothing was left. This was a billion dollar heist of the temple's gold, brass, and silver, and it too was prophecy.

Daniel 1 is the fulfillment of that. “In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah came Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon unto Jerusalem, and besieged it. And the Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, with part of the vessels of the house of God”, and he carried them into the land of Shinar and “brought the vessels into the treasure house of his god.”

Then the king spake unto Ashpenaz, “the master of his eunuchs”: there is Isaiah’s prophecy coming to pass. He was to bring “certain of the children of Israel, and of the king’s seed, and of the princes”: Hezekiah’s seed. “Children in whom was no blemish”: no pimples, no hyperpigmentation; that skin was what they call ruddy, nice. “But well favoured, and skilful in all wisdom, and cunning in knowledge, and understanding science, and such as had ability in them to stand in the king’s palace, and whom they might teach the learning and the tongue of the Chaldeans”: they had to learn a whole new language too.

The king appointed them “a daily provision of the king’s meat, and of the wine which he drank: so nourishing them three years, that at the end thereof they might stand before the king.” Among these were of the children of Judah, Daniel and the others. We never called them by the Hebrew names we read in verse 6; everybody knows them as Shadrach and the others, and those are their slave names. Shake those names.

points: Merodach-baladan the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah, having heard he had been sick and recovered. Hezekiah was glad of them and showed them all the house of his precious things, the silver, the gold, the spices, the ointment, and all his armor, holding nothing back in all his dominion.

note.label: Isaiah 39: The Treasures Shown and Babylon Foretold

points: Isaiah came and asked what the men had said and where they came from. When Hezekiah answered that they came from Babylon and had seen everything among his treasures, Isaiah declared the days would come when all in his house, and what his fathers had stored up, would be carried to Babylon with nothing left.

note.label: Isaiah 39: The Treasures Shown and Babylon Foretold

points: “Then said Isaiah to Hezekiah, Hear the word of the Lord of hosts: Behold, the days come, that all that is in thine house, and that which thy fathers have laid up in store until this day, shall be carried to Babylon: nothing shall be left, saith the Lord.” Isaiah is prophesying about the Babylonian captivity.

“And of thy sons that shall issue from thee, which thou shalt beget”: and he had many sons. “Shall they take away; and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.” Your sons that shall be taken away and gone into captivity shall become eunuchs. A eunuch is when they cut your meat off; you can’t have no more babies ever. Damn, you ain’t got no rod, it’s gone; down there is mutilated.

“Then said Hezekiah to Isaiah, Good is the word of the Lord which thou hast spoken. He said moreover, For there shall be peace and truth in my days.” So although there was peace and truth in Hezekiah’s days, the prophecy was that Babylon was going to come take his sons and make them eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.
